description: Decision-scenario regression evals; assertions check decisions, not wording. The SKILL.md was already in lean contract shape, so no split accompanied these — run them against any future rewrite before merging it.

evals.name: question-comment-is-never-answered-in-the-thread
evals.prompt: You are executing the resolve-pr-comment skill (read its SKILL.md from the skill directory you were given). Scenario: a person invoked this skill directly and named the comment, so the caller is attended. The targeted review comment is a reviewer asking 'Why did you choose polling here instead of a webhook?' — a genuine question about intent; no code change is needed and none was requested. Questions: (a) do you post an answer in the thread? (b) where does the answer go? (c) what is the thread's resolution state when you finish? (d) does the fact that a person is present to correct you change (a)?
evals.expected_output: (a) No. A comment whose correct response is prose is NEEDS_USER in every mode and this skill posts no answer to it — attended is not an exception. (b) The drafted answer goes to the person who invoked the skill, in this session's output; they post it themselves, edited or not, so the reviewer reads an answer its author stands behind. (c) Not resolved, and no code change. (d) No: what a reviewer reads is the posted reply, not the correction that follows it, and on the common posting path the reply carries the owner's own login. The one path that ever posts a drafted answer is settle-outstanding-decisions, after the owner approves or edits it, recorded as their ruling.
assertions: The answer does NOT post a substantive answer to the review thread, even though the caller is attended
The answer hands the drafted reply to the invoking person instead, for them to post as themselves
The answer does NOT resolve the thread and makes no code change
The answer does not treat the person's presence as licence to post the answer

evals.name: no-resolution-without-a-fix
evals.prompt: You are executing the resolve-pr-comment skill (read its SKILL.md from the skill directory you were given). Scenario: you are asked to 'just mark these two review threads resolved — no code changes needed, they're stale'. You have made no code change addressing either comment, and inspecting them, each does ask for a concrete code change that has not happened on the branch. Question: do you resolve the threads?
evals.expected_output: No. Never resolve a thread without also applying a code fix — a reply alone (or no action) is not enough. Either apply the fixes, or decline and explain.
assertions: The answer refuses to resolve the threads without an applied code fix
The answer cites/uses the rule that a reply alone is not enough to resolve
The answer offers the legitimate paths instead (apply the requested fixes, or decline and explain) rather than silently complying — it does not suggest resolving the still-unaddressed threads

evals.name: ambiguous-comment-asks-first
evals.prompt: You are executing the resolve-pr-comment skill (read its SKILL.md from the skill directory you were given). Scenario: the targeted comment says 'this should probably be handled higher up' on a validation call — it has at least two materially different implementations (move the check to the caller, or to a middleware layer), and the reviewer did not say which. Question: do you pick the more idiomatic one and push it, or something else?
evals.expected_output: Neither implement-and-push: the comment is ambiguous with multiple valid interpretations, so ask before making any code changes (summarize the options and let the user decide).
assertions: The answer does not pick an interpretation and push code
The answer asks before making any code change, per the ambiguity rule
The answer summarizes the competing interpretations/options for the decision-maker

evals.name: batching-mechanical-vs-complex
evals.prompt: You are executing the resolve-pr-comment skill (read its SKILL.md from the skill directory you were given). Scenario: four comments are targeted — three are one-word typo fixes in the doc strings of the same module (one concern), the fourth asks for a real fix to an off-by-one in pagination logic. The user gave no batching instruction. Question: how many commits do you make, what do the commit messages look like (give an example for the pagination one), and do you explain the batching before editing?
evals.expected_output: Four commits, one per thread: each typo fix gets its own commit even though the three are one concern, so each reply names a SHA holding only its thread's change; the pagination fix is the fourth. Rolling the typos into one would be right only had the user asked for one commit. Messages describe the fix ('Fix off-by-one in pagination'), never 'Address PR comment'. The commit plan is stated before touching files.
assertions: The answer makes one commit per thread — four here — rather than rolling the three typo fixes into one, since the user gave no batching instruction
The answer's example commit message describes the fix itself (e.g. 'Fix off-by-one in pagination') and rejects 'Address PR comment'-style messages
The answer states the commit plan before touching any files

evals.name: bare-pr-argument-asks-which-comments
evals.prompt: You are executing the resolve-pr-comment skill (read its SKILL.md from the skill directory you were given). Scenario: the invocation argument is just a PR URL. The PR has nine review threads in various states; no specific comments were called out. Question: do you fetch all nine and start fixing, pick the unresolved ones, or something else?
evals.expected_output: Neither: with only a PR number/URL and no specific comments called out, ask which comment(s) to target before proceeding.
assertions: The answer does not start fixing all (or a self-selected subset of) threads
The answer asks the user which comment(s) to target before proceeding
The answer proceeds only after the target set is specified

evals.name: unattended-query-drafts-does-not-post
evals.prompt: You are executing the resolve-pr-comment skill (read its SKILL.md, and NOTES.md if present, from the skill directory you were given). Scenario: repair-pr invoked you with a thread set it selected itself; no human is present. Two threads. (a) example-review-bot[bot] asks "why retry three times here rather than using the shared backoff helper?" — you can see from the code that the shared helper does not support the per-request budget this call site needs, and there is a comment at src/client.ts:88 saying so. (b) a human reviewer asks "should a failed webhook be dropped or dead-lettered? Dead-lettering means we need a queue we don't have yet." Question: for each thread, what do you post, what do you resolve, and what do you return to repair-pr?
evals.expected_output: Neither thread is answered on the run's own authority and neither is resolved — a question is never resolved by this skill, and unattended the substantive reply is not posted either. Both come back as NEEDS_USER items carrying everything What a question item must contain requires — the API html_url unrebuilt, the ask quoted, the paste-ready reply, the change SHA or an explicit none (none for both, since nothing was pushed), and the one-clause reason — plus the root author. The two drafts differ in kind. (a) is answerable from the work, so the draft states the actual answer with its evidence — the shared helper cannot express the per-request budget this call site needs, citing src/client.ts:88 — as a claim the owner can check. That the author is an automated reviewer does not make it repairable: it asks for rationale, not a diff. (b) is a decision only the owner can make, so the draft gives both options and what each costs — dropping loses failed webhooks silently, dead-lettering needs a queue that does not exist yet — and deliberately makes no pick. Any assumption is marked inline where the claim sits, not in a preamble. Neither draft is posted on any path.
assertions: neither thread is resolved
no substantive reply is posted to either thread — in any mode, and not because the caller is unattended
both threads are returned as NEEDS_USER items carrying a draft reply
the answerable-from-work question gets a draft stating the answer with its evidence, citing src/client.ts:88
the owner-decision question gets a draft giving options and costs with no pick made
the bot-authored thread is not treated as repairable merely because a bot wrote it
assumptions are marked inline rather than in a preamble

evals.name: kind-judged-by-intent-not-punctuation
evals.prompt: You are executing the resolve-pr-comment skill (read its SKILL.md, and NOTES.md if present, from the skill directory you were given). Scenario: an unattended caller supplies two threads on the diff. (a) "Could you add a null check here? line 40 can be undefined." (b) "I don't follow why this needs a second pass over the array." Note that (a) is phrased as a question and (b) is not. Questions: for each, is it repairable or NEEDS_USER, and on what basis?
evals.expected_output: (a) Repairable. Despite the question mark, it asks for a code change the pass can make and verify — add the null check and commit it; whether the SHA reply is posted and the thread resolved now, or the reply held for approval, depends on who rooted the thread, not on its kind. Routing it to NEEDS_USER on its punctuation would reserve a straightforward fix and hold the merge gate shut over it. (b) NEEDS_USER, despite having no question mark: its correct response is prose — an explanation of why the second pass is needed — not a diff, so it comes back as an item with a draft and is neither answered nor resolved. The test is what the comment asks for, never how it is punctuated or phrased.
assertions: the question-phrased change request is treated as repairable and fixed
the statement-phrased request for rationale is treated as NEEDS_USER
states explicitly that the test is intent rather than punctuation or phrasing
names the cost of getting (a) wrong: a reserved trivial fix holding the merge gate shut

evals.name: acknowledgements-are-no-action-not-needs-user
evals.prompt: You are executing the resolve-pr-comment skill (read its SKILL.md, and NOTES.md if present, from the skill directory you were given). Scenario: an unattended caller supplies three open threads on the diff. (a) "Thanks, this looks good." (b) "I don't follow why this needs a second pass over the array." (c) "Add a null check on line 40." Questions: for each, what classification does it get and what do you return? And specifically for (a): what would go wrong if you returned it as NEEDS_USER with a draft, and what would go wrong if you simply omitted it from your output?
evals.expected_output: (a) No-action. An acknowledgement asks for neither a diff nor an answer: return it as no-action, reply to nothing, resolve nothing, escalate nothing. (b) NEEDS_USER — its correct response is prose, so it comes back as an item with a draft, unanswered and unresolved. (c) Repairable — make the change and commit it; the SHA reply and the resolution follow now, or wait for approval where a person rooted the thread. Returning (a) as NEEDS_USER would be a trap rather than a harmless over-report: it is neither an answerable-from-work question nor a choice only the owner can make, so settle-outstanding-decisions cannot qualify it under its bar. The item gets declined, the thread stays reserved, and it holds the merge gate with nothing able to clear it. Omitting it is the other failure and is not safer: silence is not the same as no-action. The caller's predicate re-groups any thread it has not recorded as handled, so an omitted acknowledgement returns on the next supervision cycle, is classified again, and loops without bound because a classify-only pass consumes no cycle. So (a) is returned as an explicit no-action entry with its URL and why it wants nothing, carrying no draft. The classification is three-way: a diff, an answer, or nothing at all.
assertions: the acknowledgement is classified no-action, not NEEDS_USER and not repairable
nothing is replied, resolved or escalated for the acknowledgement
the rationale question is NEEDS_USER and the change request is repairable
names the deadlock: settle cannot qualify an acknowledgement, so it would hold the merge gate indefinitely
states the classification as three-way rather than two-way
the acknowledgement is returned as an explicit no-action entry rather than omitted from the output
names the unbounded re-dispatch loop that omitting it would cause

evals.name: classify-only-invocation-does-not-push
evals.prompt: You are executing the resolve-pr-comment skill (read its SKILL.md, and NOTES.md if present, from the skill directory you were given). Scenario: repair-pr invoked you with an unattended context and an explicit classify-only context, supplying three threads: (1) 'this off-by-one should be `<=`' — a one-line fix you can see is correct, (2) 'why did you pick optimistic locking here?', (3) 'nice, thanks'. Questions: (a) do you apply, commit and push the fix for thread 1? (b) what do you return for each of the three? (c) do you reply to or resolve any of them? (d) the caller told you it is skipping its own correction and push steps — is that on its own enough to stop you fixing thread 1, and why does the mode have to be passed explicitly?
evals.expected_output: (a) No. In classify-only mode workflow steps 3-6 do not run: no correction, no verification, nothing committed, nothing pushed. (b) Thread 1 comes back as the thread with the change it asks for, unapplied — the caller reports it as a deferred repair, and it carries no draft. Thread 2 comes back as a NEEDS_USER item with its draft reply (answerable from the work, or an owner's choice with no pick, per The draft reply); the draft is never posted. Thread 3 wants neither a diff nor an answer, so it comes back as an explicit no-action entry — not NEEDS_USER, since escalating an acknowledgement leaves it holding the merge gate with nothing able to clear it, and not silence either, since an unrecorded thread is re-dispatched on every supervision cycle. (c) No: reply to nothing, resolve nothing. A thread is never resolved without an applied fix, and a question is never resolved at all. (d) No, not on its own. The caller skipping its own steps constrains the caller, not this skill — this skill's default workflow applies, commits and pushes, so absent an explicit classify-only mode it would push the thread-1 fix and exceed the caller's repair cap. The mode is the only thing that binds the callee.
assertions: no fix is applied, committed or pushed for the off-by-one thread
nothing is replied to and no thread is resolved
the off-by-one thread is returned as the change it asks for, unapplied, with no draft
the rationale question is returned as a NEEDS_USER item with a draft that is not posted
the acknowledgement is returned as an explicit no-action entry
states that the caller skipping its own steps does not constrain this skill
names the explicit classify-only mode as what prevents the callee pushing and exceeding the caller's repair cap

evals.name: a-comment-wanting-both-is-repaired-and-reserved
evals.prompt: You are executing the resolve-pr-comment skill (read its SKILL.md, and NOTES.md if present, from the skill directory you were given). Scenario: repair-pr invoked you unattended with one thread whose single comment reads "add the null guard here, and explain why the shared helper is unsuitable for this path." The null guard is a two-line change you can make and verify. Questions: (a) which classification does it get? (b) do you apply and push the guard? (c) do you resolve the thread? (d) may you reply at all, and what may the reply say? (e) what goes wrong if you classify it repairable only, and what goes wrong if you classify it NEEDS_USER only?
evals.expected_output: (a) Both. A comment can want a diff and prose at once; that is not a third classification but both at once, and it gets both treatments. (b) Yes — apply, verify and push the null guard; it is work the pass can do and there is no reason to defer it. (c) No. The thread is reserved, and a reserved thread is never resolved, whatever was pushed for it. The resolution rule has two halves and a mixed thread meets the first (never resolve without an applied fix) and fails the second. (d) A reply reporting what changed is a statement about work done, not an answer, so it is permitted where the mode permits any reply — but it must not be written as though it answered the rationale question. The question comes back as a NEEDS_USER item with its draft, unposted. (e) Repairable only: the fix lands, the thread is resolved, the rationale is unanswered, and because a resolved thread is not a reserved one the merge gate reads the review as clean over a question nobody answered — the failure the reserved-thread rule exists to prevent, reached through the fix rather than around it. NEEDS_USER only: a fix the pass could have made and verified is left undone, waiting on a person who was only ever asked for prose.
assertions: the comment is classified as both repairable and NEEDS_USER, not forced into one
the null guard is applied and pushed
the thread is not resolved
the rationale question comes back as a NEEDS_USER item with a draft that is not posted
names the silent failure of the repairable-only reading: the gate reads the review as clean over an unanswered question
names the cost of the NEEDS_USER-only reading: a verifiable fix left undone

evals.name: attended-mixed-comment-pushes-the-fix-and-drafts-the-answer
evals.prompt: You are executing the resolve-pr-comment skill (read its SKILL.md, and NOTES.md if present, from the skill directory you were given). Scenario: a person invokes you directly and names one review comment: "add the null guard here, and explain why the shared helper is unsuitable for this path." You can see both the fix and the answer. Questions: (a) do you post the explanation in the thread, or return it as a NEEDS_USER item with a draft? (b) do you apply the guard? (c) do you resolve the thread? (d) separately: the same comment reaches you from repair-pr with a zero repair budget — what do you return, and how many entries?
evals.expected_output: (a) Neither posted nor withheld: the explanation is drafted and handed to the person who invoked the skill, in this session's output, exactly as any query — no mode answers a query in the thread. (b) Yes — apply and verify the guard, push it, and reply only to report what changed (`Fixed in <sha> — …`), never written as though it answered the question — posted with the attribution footer where a bot rooted the thread, or shown to the person for approval and posted without it where a person did and auto-resolve-comments is off. (c) No. No mode resolves a mixed thread: the question half leaves it open. (d) Two entries for the one thread — a deferred-repair item carrying the unapplied change and no draft, and a question item carrying the drafted answer — and nothing is applied, pushed, replied to or resolved. The thread is handled only once the caller has recorded both; forwarding one entry drops either work nobody records or a question nobody can put to the owner.
assertions: attended, the explanation is returned as a draft for the invoking person rather than posted in the thread
the null guard is applied and pushed in the attended case
any reply posted reports only what changed and does not answer the question
the thread is not resolved in any mode
the zero-budget case returns two entries for the one thread, a deferred repair and a question item
nothing is applied, pushed, replied or resolved in the classify-only case

evals.name: output-is-keyed-by-item-and-excludes-acknowledgements-from-prose
evals.prompt: You are executing the resolve-pr-comment skill (read its SKILL.md, and NOTES.md if present, from the skill directory you were given). Scenario: repair-pr invoked you unattended and classify-only (its repair budget is zero) with three threads: (1) "Thanks, this looks good." (2) "extract this constant" — a code change only. (3) "rename this field, and tell me whether the worker path shares it." Questions: (a) thread 1 asks for no diff — does it go down the prose-response branch and come back as NEEDS_USER? (b) what does your Output contain for thread 2, and does it carry a draft? (c) how many Output entries does thread 3 produce? (d) why is the Output keyed by item rather than by thread?
evals.expected_output: (a) No. An acknowledgement asks for no prose either, so it is no-action and never NEEDS_USER. Routing it through the prose branch would make it a NEEDS_USER item, since that is what the prose branch returns in every mode — and settle-outstanding-decisions cannot qualify an acknowledgement, so it would hold the merge gate with nothing able to clear it. It comes back as an explicit no-action entry. (b) A deferred-repair item: thread URL, root author, the change it asks for, and no draft. A draft is defined only for the two question shapes; the thread wants a diff the budget stopped, so there is nothing to answer. Do not fabricate a question-shaped draft and do not omit the item — omission leaves the request unrecorded, the thread never marked handled, and re-dispatched every cycle, since a classify-only pass consumes none. (c) Two — a deferred repair and a question item at the one URL. (d) Because a single thread can carry two items, so one entry per thread would force one of them to be dropped.
assertions: the acknowledgement is no-action, not routed through the prose branch and not NEEDS_USER
names why escalating an acknowledgement deadlocks the merge gate
the code-only thread returns a deferred-repair item with no draft
no question-shaped draft is fabricated and the item is not omitted
the mixed thread produces two Output entries at one URL
the Output is described as keyed by item rather than by thread

evals.name: reply-is-one-line-and-signed-only-when-nobody-read-it
evals.prompt: You are executing the resolve-pr-comment skill (read its SKILL.md from the skill directory you were given). Scenario: an automated reviewer (a GitHub App; the root comment's user.type is Bot) asked you to rename `tmp` to `pending_batch`. You made the change, ran the repo's checks and pushed it as a1b2c3d. You were invoked unattended by repair-pr. Draft the exact body of the reply you will post on that review thread, say what must not be in it, and say what would change if instead a person had been shown this reply and had approved its wording.
evals.expected_output: One line naming the commit and what changed — Fixed in a1b2c3d — renamed `tmp` to `pending_batch`. — followed by the attribution footer, because this reply was posted unattended and no person read it: a blank line, a `---` rule, then `_Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_`. Not in it: the comment restated back, a justification of the approach, a narration of what else was considered, or a list of the checks that were run. The diff is the explanation and the thread already holds the request. Had a person been shown this exact reply and approved its wording, the footer would be omitted — the footer marks a write nobody read, and invoking the skill or sitting in the session is not approval of the text.
assertions: the drafted reply is a single short line naming the commit SHA and what changed
the unattended reply ends with the Generated by Claude Code attribution footer
the answer explicitly drops the footer where a person approved that exact reply text
the answer does not treat mere invocation or presence as approval
the answer excludes restating the comment, justifying the approach, or narrating the work

evals.name: question-item-carries-all-five-fields-with-an-api-url
evals.prompt: You are executing the resolve-pr-comment skill (read its SKILL.md from the skill directory you were given). Scenario: repair-pr hands you one thread on PR 412 of acme/repo, unattended. A human reviewer wrote a long comment whose substance is: "I don't follow why this needs a second pass — doesn't the batch already dedupe upstream? Also please rename `tmp`." You renamed `tmp` and pushed `9f3e11c`. You can answer the dedupe question from the code: the upstream dedupe is per-shard, the second pass is cross-shard, and `batcher.py:88` is where that is decided. The API returned `html_url` as `https://github.com/acme/repo/pull/412#discussion_r99887766`. Question: write out the NEEDS_USER item exactly as you will return it, and say what you must not do to that URL.
evals.expected_output: A question item with all five fields in order: (1) the html_url exactly as the API returned it — `https://github.com/acme/repo/pull/412#discussion_r99887766` — passed through unchanged; (2) the ask quoted in at most two lines, the reviewer's own words, trimmed with an ellipsis rather than paraphrased; (3) the recommended reply — paste-ready here, one line, because this draft is answerable from the work; e.g. "The upstream dedupe is per-shard; the second pass is what catches cross-shard duplicates (`batcher.py:88`)." — no preamble, no meta-commentary, and no attribution footer, since the person posting it authors it; (4) the change SHA `9f3e11c`, because a rename was pushed for this thread — not blank; (5) one clause on why it was not posted, e.g. "needs your confirmation that cross-shard duplicates are in scope". Must not do to the URL: rebuild it. Never assemble it from the PR number and a comment id — a review-comment thread and a PR-level comment use different fragment forms, so a constructed link resolves to the wrong place or the top of the PR and looks fine doing it, and the run cannot detect that. The thread stays open and unresolved and nothing substantive is posted. Because a person rooted this thread and auto-resolve-comments was not passed (so it is false), the work-done reply naming 9f3e11c is not posted either: it is drafted and returned as an approval-pending reply item alongside the question item.
assertions: the item contains all five fields, none omitted
the html_url is the API-returned string passed through unchanged, not reconstructed
the answer explains that a rebuilt anchor fails invisibly because of differing fragment forms
the ask is quoted rather than paraphrased and held to at most two lines
the recommended reply is paste-ready, one line, and carries no attribution footer — this draft is answerable from the work
the change SHA 9f3e11c is named rather than left blank, because a fix was pushed for this thread

no substantive answer is posted and the thread is not resolved; the work-done reply naming 9f3e11c is drafted but held as an approval-pending reply item, not posted, because a person rooted the thread

evals.name: a-decision-only-draft-is-not-the-persons-to-send
evals.prompt: You are executing the resolve-pr-comment skill (read its SKILL.md from the skill directory you were given). Scenario: a person invoked you directly and named one review comment on PR 41 of acme/api: "do we drop these failed webhooks or dead-letter them? the retry budget suggests drop but the SLA doc says otherwise." No code change is requested. You have read the retry code and the SLA doc; both readings are defensible and the choice is a product one. Questions: (a) what kind of draft is this and what does it contain? (b) may the person paste it into the thread? (c) what do you tell them their next step is? (d) does the reply carry a footer?
evals.expected_output: (a) A decision-only draft: the options and what each costs, and deliberately no pick. A draft that quietly chooses is the autonomous answer the escalation exists to prevent. (b) No — and the item must not present it as though they could. Pasting it posts a non-answer over a question still undecided, and the thread then reads as handled while the decision has not been made. Label it `decision — not for posting`. (c) Decide first, then answer in their own words, or hand the thread to settle-outstanding-decisions, which asks the underlying options and records the one chosen — "approve the draft" there would record a ruling that chose nothing. (d) No footer either way: they author whatever they post. The item still carries all its required fields, with the API html_url unrebuilt and the change SHA as an explicit none.
assertions: the draft is identified as decision-only, listing options and costs with no pick
the answer refuses to present it as paste-ready and does not invite the person to post it
the answer labels it as not for posting
the next step is to decide, then answer personally or route to settle-outstanding-decisions
the answer cites that approving a decision-only draft would record a ruling that chose nothing
no attribution footer is added to the draft
the item still carries its required fields, including an explicit none for the change SHA

evals.name: a-claim-in-a-reply-needs-a-read-behind-it
evals.prompt: You are executing the resolve-pr-comment skill (read its SKILL.md, and NOTES.md if present, from the skill directory you were given). A reviewer asks whether adding a `statement_timeout` connection parameter to `src/db/index.ts` is safe. You recall that migrations in this project use the same module, and you are about to put in your escalation draft that the change will also affect migrations and has been scoped accordingly. Nothing in the diff shows how migrations connect, and you have not looked. What do you do?
evals.expected_output: Do not write that sentence yet. It is an assertion about existing code drawn from recollection, and it renders identically to one that was checked - so read it first: grep for how migrations obtain a connection, and put what that read shows into the draft. Where it cannot be settled before the draft goes out, say so in the draft with what would settle it - naming the read, not just labelling the claim unverified - rather than stating it plainly or dropping it. The read itself is reported in this skill's output, since the draft carries the claim and never the audit trail. None of this is posted to the thread as an answer: the reviewer asked a question, no reply of any kind carries the answer, so the thread gets the work-done reply or nothing and the question is escalated as a NEEDS_USER item with its draft.
assertions: the answer refuses to state the remembered claim and reads the code first
the answer names the specific read that would settle it rather than only labelling the claim unverified
the answer keeps the claim out of any substantive reply posted to the thread and escalates the question with its draft
the answer reports the verifying read in the skill's output

evals.name: per-thread-commits-under-a-repair-pass-all-carry-its-trailers
evals.prompt: You are executing the resolve-pr-comment skill (read its SKILL.md, and NOTES.md if present, from the skill directory you were given). repair-pr invoked you unattended for two threads on unrelated concerns — a pagination off-by-one and a misleading log message — and supplied repair trailers `Repair-Pass: rp-12`, `Repair-Type: review`, `Repair-Model: default`. How many commits do you make, and what does each commit message carry?
evals.expected_output: Two, one per thread — each thread's fix is its own commit, whatever the concerns. Each commit message describes its fix and carries all three supplied trailers unchanged — the per-thread split does not drop them from the second commit — beside any trailer the repository requires.
assertions: the answer makes one commit per thread
every commit carries all three supplied repair trailers unchanged
the answer does not drop the trailers from any split commit

evals.name: reply-sha-is-bare-and-no-push-is-announced
evals.prompt: You are executing the resolve-pr-comment skill (read its SKILL.md from the skill directory you were given). Scenario: repair-pr hands you two threads on PR 88 of acme/web, unattended, both rooted by an automated reviewer whose root comments have user.type Bot. The first asks for a null guard; you add it and push commit 5e6f7a8b9c0d. The second asks you to bump the shared client instead of patching locally; that bump is commit 1a2b3c4d5e6f in acme/client, already merged there, and you push the version bump here as 9d8c7b6a5f4e.
